items.title: Foreigners accused of visa overstay can't be kept in detention centres after getting bail: Delhi High Court
items.summary: The Delhi High Court has ruled that foreign nationals accused of overstaying their visas cannot be directed to remain in detention centres as a condition for being granted bail. A Bench of Justices Navin Chawla and Arun Bhardwaj said that imposing such a condition would defeat the very purpose of granting bail. It added that foreign nationals accused of violating immigration laws are entitled to be considered for bail in the same manner as other criminal accused. “A direction imposing a condition wherein the foreign national is restricted to a detention centre would frustrate the very order of bail and hence, cannot be imposed. Such a power can be exercised by the Central Government by an order under Section 3(2)(g) of the 1946 Act [Foreigners Act], or under Paragraph 8 of the Immigration and Foreigners Order, 2025,” the Court said. However, it clarified that granting bail does not legalise a foreign national's continued stay in India or operate as a substitute for a valid visa. The Coram of President Satpal and Members Dr Sushma Garg and Dr Suman Singh held that the unilateral wallet adjustment amounted to a deceptive "dark pattern" and deficiency in service under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019. On both occasions, a Munch Max chocolate bar priced at ₹19 was unavailable. In the chargesheet, the agency had stated that 3 subject experts leaked the NEET exam questions from the National Testing Agency (NTA) office in Delhi through different methods. items.title: Senior Advocate Darius Khambata hits back at Tata Trusts vice-chairpersons over listing u-turn
items.summary: Senior Advocate and former Tata Trusts trustee Darius J Khambata has rebutted allegations levelled against him by Tata Trusts Vice-Chairmen Venu Srinivasan and Vijay Singh and questioned their sudden shift in stance on the public listing of Tata Sons. In a four-page letter dated November 17, Khambata categorically rejected the personal attacks against him. “I categorically reject the accusations you make against me in your letter. They selectively cite events excluding critical facts to construct a false narrative," he said. The exchange follows Khambata’s decision earlier this month not to seek reappointment as a trustee. In a November 2 letter to Chairman Noel Tata and CEO Siddharth Sharma, he had warned that the Tata Group's governance model was under threat over the proposed listing of Tata Sons. He had also criticised the events of the September 17 board meeting as “a day that will live in infamy". In his latest communication, Khambata expressed disappointment that Srinivasan and Singh's November 13 letter failed to explain their change in position as regards the proposed public listing of the company. According to Khambata, the two were earlier against the listing of Tata Son

items.title: Kerala High Court asks media to be cautious while reporting oral remarks made by judges in court
items.summary: The Kerala High Court on Tuesday observed that the media should exercise restraint while reporting oral remarks made by judges during court proceedings, particularly when the circulation of such remarks could tarnish the image of lawyers or judges [ TB Mini v The Hon'ble Registrar General & ors ]. Justice PV Kunhikrishnan observed that judges and lawyers sometimes exchange jokes or make casual remarks during proceedings to ease the atmosphere in the courtroom. However, such informal conversations should remain within the courtroom, the Court said while urging the media to restrain from reporting such exchanges in a manner that could damage the reputation of the judges or lawyers involved. " Judges or lawyers may not intend any harm when they make comments or jokes in court, because a serious courtroom, where only interpretations of law and facts are discussed, can be boring for Judges, lawyers, and litigants, and a joke can ease the mood and atmosphere. Therefore, it is improper for the media to cover such dialogues between a lawyer and a Judge in a way that tarnishes the image of a lawyer or a Judge. items.title: Calcutta High Court upholds death penalty of man for rape and murder of 5-year-old girl
items.summary: The Calcutta High Court on Tuesday upheld the death penalty of a man found guilty of raping and subsequently murdering his neighbour's five- year-old daughter after luring her with chocolates [ State of West Bengal v. Ashok Singh] . A Bench of Justices Arijit Banerjee and Apurba Sinha Ray noted that the convict Ashok Singh raped the child through her vagina as well as anus and later killed the child by inflicting injuries on her head. His actions could plainly be classified into the "rarest of rare" category, thus fitting the criteria to attract a death sentence, the Court ruled. "The manner of raping a 5 years 10 months old child through her vagina and also her anus were sufficient to take the life of the child but to ensure her total collapse he banged her head against hard substance. In my view, the death of the victim was done with extreme depravity and this brutal nature of rape and murder of the 5 years 10 months old child, is in my view, qualifies as one of the rarest of the rare cases," the judgment said. The Court was hearing an appeal preferred by Ashok Singh challenging an order of a trial court which had sentenced him to death. The crime took place on November 24, 2024
